title: Act V, Scene VI

teacherSummary.text: Before Dunsinane, Malcolm orders the soldiers to throw down their 'leavy screens' and show themselves as they are. His uncle Siward and Siward's son will lead the first battle; Malcolm and Macduff will do the rest. Macduff calls for all the trumpets to sound, 'those clamorous harbingers of blood and death.'

Malcolm tells the soldiers they are near enough to stop hiding and show themselves. His uncle Siward and Siward's son will lead the first attack, while he and Macduff will handle whatever else remains, as they have planned. The orders are clear and calm, showing a well-organized army ready for battle.

Siward says that if they find Macbeth's forces that night and cannot fight, they deserve to be beaten. Macduff calls for every trumpet to sound loudly, announcing bloodshed and death. Both speak in rhyming couplets that sound firm and final, showing they are eager to face the tyrant at last.
